_note: TEMPLATE. Copy to profile.json and fill it in: `cp data/profile.example.json data/profile.json`, then run `python -m core.profile checkfill` to list everything still unset. Anything left as FILL_ME is treated as MISSING — the extension will not autofill it and will surface the question instead of guessing, which is the intended failure mode. Booleans render as Yes/No via core/profile.py.

identity._location_display_note: How a single-box location field should read. Many ATS location pickers search server-side on what is typed, so use the form their dropdown expects, e.g. 'City, State, Country'.

_work_authorization_note: REVIEW EVERY VALUE HERE BEFORE YOUR FIRST RUN. These answers are submitted to real employers and a wrong default is worse than no answer. The booleans below are only placeholders to show the shape, not a recommendation.

education._school_note: Use the school's full formal name and avoid parentheticals/acronyms. ATS school pickers run a server-side search on exactly this string, and a bracketed acronym returns zero matches — see the type-to-search notes in extension/fill.js.

preferences._target_roles_note: Free text, used to ground Claude-drafted essay answers (bridge/drafter.py). Say what you are aiming FOR, e.g. 'backend and platform engineering roles in the US'.
preferences.work_arrangement: Open to remote, hybrid, or onsite

attestations._note: Yes/No attestation-style questions. Booleans render Yes/No. Defaults below are the common case, but they are ASSERTIONS ABOUT YOU — read every one.

eeo._note: US voluntary self-identification. Left as FILL_ME on purpose: there is no sane default for someone else's demographics, and every field here is optional on the form. Fill in what you want auto-answered and leave the rest — anything unset is simply surfaced for you to answer by hand. Declining is always a valid answer; most forms offer a 'I don't wish to answer' option you can paste in verbatim.

affiliations._note: Prior/related-connection disclosure questions. All No assumes you are not applying to a current or former employer, or to a company where you have a relative. If you ever do, add a per-company override in taxonomy.yaml so it gets surfaced instead of auto-answered.

_local_resume_source._note: Resumes are copied from this LOCAL folder into the gitignored resumes/ cache that the extension reads for its DataTransfer attach. Point base_dir at wherever your PDFs live, then run `python -m core.resumes sync-local`. Each track's local_source is relative to base_dir.

_resume_tracks_note: One resume per specialisation; the scraper picks a track per role by keyword overlap against the job title and description (title weighted 2x). Keep 1 track if you only have one resume — set its keywords to [] and make it default_resume_tag. The keyword lists below are generic and safe to keep as-is. drive_id is optional and only used by the Google Drive sync path.
